scheme_name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro & Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
description: Provides collateral-free credit guarantee to MSEs through member lending institutions. No third-party guarantee required. Over 60 lakh guarantees issued since inception.
procedure: Step 1: Register your business on Udyam Portal (udyamregistration.gov.in) and obtain Udyam Registration Number.
Step 2: Approach any CGTMSE Member Lending Institution (MLI) — PSU banks, private banks, NBFCs, or SFBs.
Step 3: Submit loan application with business plan, financial projections, and KYC documents to the bank.
Step 4: Bank appraises the loan proposal and forwards it to CGTMSE for guarantee coverage.
Step 5: CGTMSE issues guarantee approval; bank sanctions and disburses loan without collateral.
Step 6: Pay Annual Guarantee Fee (AGF) as applicable (0.37%–1.35% of loan amount per year).
Step 7: Maintain regular loan repayments; in case of default, bank files claim with CGTMSE.
documents_required: PAN Card of Business and Owner
Last 2 years ITR and Balance Sheet (for existing units)
eligibility_criteria: Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) with valid Udyam Registration.
Both new and existing businesses eligible.
Loan amount up to ₹5 crore covered.
Manufacturing or service sector.
No wilful defaulter status.
notes: CGTMSE guarantee is availed by the bank on behalf of the borrower — the applicant does not apply directly to CGTMSE.
Guarantee fee is paid by the borrower as part of loan terms.
Coverage is 75%–85% of loan amount depending on borrower category.

description: Micro-finance for very small and new businesses. No collateral required. Targeted at street vendors, artisans, and first-generation micro entrepreneurs.
procedure: Step 1: Visit nearest bank branch (PSU, private, RRB, MFI, NBFC-MFI, cooperative bank) or apply on Udyamimitra portal (udyamimitra.in).
Step 2: Fill MUDRA Loan Application Form (Shishu) with business details and loan requirement.
Step 3: Submit KYC documents and business proof to the bank/MFI.
Step 4: Bank processes application; for Shishu loans most lenders have simplified in-branch processing.
Step 5: Loan is sanctioned (typically within 7–14 working days for Shishu category).
Step 6: Receive loan disbursement directly to bank account.
Step 7: A MUDRA Card (RuPay Debit Card) is issued for working capital drawdown as needed.
documents_required: Proof of business address (rent agreement / utility bill)
eligibility_criteria: Any Indian citizen engaged in non-farm, non-corporate income-generating activity.
Loan amount up to ₹50,000.
First-time borrowers, street vendors, artisans, small traders.
No prior MUDRA loan default.
No minimum income bar.
notes: Shishu loans up to ₹50,000 have the simplest documentation.
Interest rates are set by individual lending institutions.
No collateral or guarantor required.
MUDRA card allows flexible working capital withdrawal.

description: For established micro businesses seeking to expand. Covers working capital and term loan needs with minimal documentation requirements.
procedure: Step 1: Visit the lending institution (bank/MFI/NBFC) or apply online at udyamimitra.in.
Step 2: Fill Kishor MUDRA Loan Application Form specifying loan amount and purpose.
Step 3: Submit financial documents including existing business proof and 6 months bank statements.
Step 4: Bank conducts basic credit assessment and business visit if required.
Step 5: Loan is appraised and sanctioned (typically 15–21 working days).
Step 6: Execute loan agreement and receive disbursement.
Step 7: MUDRA Card issued for working capital component if applicable.
documents_required: Last 1 year ITR or business income proof
eligibility_criteria: Existing micro/small businesses with at least 6 months vintage.
Loan amount between ₹50,001 and ₹5 lakh.
No wilful default history.
Non-farm, non-corporate sector businesses.
notes: Kishor loans require slightly more documentation than Shishu due to higher amounts.
Interest rates vary by lender (typically 10–16% p.a.).
Businesses with Udyam registration get faster processing.

description: For well-established micro businesses needing higher credit. No collateral required. Competitive interest rates through partner lenders.
procedure: Step 1: Apply at a bank branch or online via udyamimitra.in. Select 'Tarun' category.
Step 2: Submit detailed business plan, financial statements, and growth projections.
Step 3: Provide complete KYC and business registration documents.
Step 4: Bank conducts thorough credit assessment including site visit.
Step 5: Credit appraisal completed; sanction letter issued (21–30 working days).
Step 6: Sign loan agreement and mortgage/hypothecation documents if required.
Step 7: Loan disbursed; MUDRA card issued for working capital component.
eligibility_criteria: Well-established micro/small enterprises.
Loan amount ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh.
Good repayment track record.
Non-farm sector.
Valid business registration.
notes: Tarun category requires more rigorous documentation.
Under Tarun Plus (above ₹10 lakh up to ₹20 lakh), additional scrutiny applies.
CGTMSE coverage available for Tarun loans.

scheme_name: PM MUDRA Yojana — Tarun Plus Category
description: Enhanced Mudra loan tier for small enterprises seeking to expand capacity with faster processing through MUDRA partner lenders.
procedure: Step 1: Approach your existing MUDRA lender with application for Tarun Plus upgrade.
Step 2: Submit updated financials showing business growth and repayment history.
Step 3: Provide business expansion plan detailing use of additional funds.
Step 4: Bank verifies existing MUDRA track record and conducts fresh credit assessment.
Step 5: Sanction letter issued after bank approval (21–30 working days).
Step 6: Execute enhanced loan agreement.
Step 7: Disbursement made; continue regular EMI repayments.
documents_required: Previous MUDRA loan statements and NOC
Last 2 years ITR and audited financials
eligibility_criteria: Must have availed and repaid MUDRA Tarun loan satisfactorily.
Loan amount ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh.
Business must show growth trajectory.
Non-farm sector.
Udyam registration mandatory.
notes: Tarun Plus is a step-up product for existing MUDRA borrowers only.
Maintain clean repayment record on previous MUDRA loan to be eligible.
CGTMSE guarantee applies.

description: Financial assistance for DPIIT-recognised startups for PoC, prototype development, product trials, and market entry through SEBI-registered incubators across India.
procedure: Step 1: Register startup on Startup India Hub (startupindia.gov.in) and obtain DPIIT recognition certificate.
Step 2: Visit SISFS portal (seedfund.startupindia.gov.in) and browse list of approved incubators.
Step 3: Apply to one or more approved incubators by submitting startup profile, pitch deck, and financial plan.
Step 4: Incubator's Experts Advisory Committee (EAC) reviews application and schedules pitch presentation.
Step 5: EAC evaluates startup and recommends grant/debt/equity support.
Step 6: Incubator forwards recommendation to DPIIT for approval.
Step 7: Funds disbursed by incubator to startup in tranches against milestones.
Step 8: Submit utilization certificates and progress reports to incubator quarterly.
documents_required: PAN Card of company and founders
eligibility_criteria: DPIIT-recognised startup incorporated ≤2 years as on date of application.
Not received more than ₹10 lakh in government funding.
Must be Indian incorporated entity (Pvt Ltd, OPC, LLP, Partnership).
Product/service with market potential.
Applied through DPIIT-approved incubators only.
notes: Startups must apply to incubators, not DPIIT directly.
Each incubator has its own selection criteria beyond SISFS guidelines.
Funds are milestone-based — maintain proper records.
Maximum grant: ₹20 lakh; debt/equity: ₹50 lakh.

description: Upfront capital subsidy of 15% on institutional credit up to ₹1 Crore for technology upgradation of Small Scale Industries. 5000+ eligible product categories.
procedure: Step 1: Register on Udyam Portal and verify your MSME falls under eligible sub-sector list (Ministry of MSME website).
Step 2: Identify approved technology/machinery from CLCSS approved list on msme.gov.in.
Step 3: Approach scheduled commercial bank / PLI (Primary Lending Institution) with technology upgrade proposal.
Step 4: Bank appraises project and sanctions term loan. Bank applies to SIDBI/NABARD (Nodal Agencies) for subsidy.
Step 5: Nodal agency (SIDBI or NABARD) verifies and releases 15% subsidy to bank.
Step 6: Bank adjusts subsidy amount against loan principal — reducing borrower's outstanding.
Step 7: Submit utilization certificate and machine invoice to bank after purchase.
documents_required: Last 3 years ITR and Balance Sheet
eligibility_criteria: Registered MSME (manufacturing) in eligible sub-sectors as notified by MSME Ministry.
Availing term loan from scheduled commercial bank/SFB/RRB/SIDBI.
Technology upgrade must be from approved list of technologies.
Both new and existing MSMEs eligible.
notes: Subsidy is 15% of loan amount — maximum subsidy ₹15 lakh (on loan up to ₹1 crore).
Subsidy is released upfront and adjusted in principal.
Technology must be from the approved list; ensure compatibility before applying.

scheme_name: SIDBI Fund of Funds — Startup India
description: ₹10,000 Crore corpus routed through SEBI-registered AIFs providing equity support to startups. Over 900 startups funded across India.
procedure: Step 1: Obtain DPIIT recognition from Startup India Hub (startupindia.gov.in).
Step 2: Connect with SEBI-registered AIF fund managers who have received SIDBI FoF allocation.
Step 3: Submit pitch deck, financial model, and business plan to the AIF.
Step 4: AIF conducts due diligence including market analysis, team assessment, financials.
Step 5: Investment committee of AIF approves investment term sheet.
Step 6: Legal documentation (SHA, SSA) executed between startup and AIF.
Step 7: Funds disbursed in tranches as per agreed milestones and reporting obligations.
documents_required: Term Sheet (if already in discussion with AIF)
eligibility_criteria: DPIIT-recognised startup.
Must be investable by SEBI-registered Category I or II AIF.
Not directly applied — accessed via VC/AIF funds.
Startup should be at growth stage with viable business model.
notes: Startups do not apply to SIDBI directly — approach SIDBI FoF empanelled AIF fund managers.
List of funds available on SIDBI website.
This is equity funding — expect dilution.
SIDBI Startup Mitra portal lists empanelled funds.

scheme_name: Atal Innovation Mission — Atal Incubation Centres (AIC)
description: World-class incubation centres across India providing mentoring, infrastructure, investor networks, and seed funding access to deep-tech startups.
procedure: Step 1: Visit AIM website (aim.gov.in) and browse list of established AICs across India.
Step 2: Identify an AIC relevant to your sector/domain and apply on the AIC's individual portal or via AIM portal.
Step 3: Submit startup idea, pitch deck, team profile, and innovation description.
Step 4: AIC selection committee reviews applications and shortlists startups.
Step 5: Attend pitch/interview session at the AIC.
Step 6: Selected startups sign incubation agreement with the AIC.
Step 7: Avail services: lab infrastructure, mentorship, investor connects, co-working space, and networking events.
documents_required: Prototype details or demo video (if available)
eligibility_criteria: Early-stage startups (idea to early revenue stage).
Must apply to specific AIC at a host institution.
Preference for innovative, technology-driven, and problem-solving startups.
No specific revenue or age bar but must have a viable innovation.
notes: Each AIC has its own cohort and selection cycle.
Some AICs offer equity-free grants up to ₹50 lakh.
AIC incubation is typically 18–24 months.
Check individual AIC websites for specific cohort timelines.

description: Financial assistance for market development, packaging, certification, and export promotion for agri-food exporters. Covers 46 scheduled products.
procedure: Step 1: Register as an exporter with APEDA at apeda.gov.in/apedawebsite/ and obtain RCMC.
Step 2: Identify the relevant assistance scheme component (transport subsidy, infrastructure, quality, market development).
Step 3: Submit online application on APEDA portal with required documents.
Step 4: APEDA verifies eligibility and documents submitted.
Step 5: Field inspection / verification conducted if required.
Step 6: Sanction order issued by APEDA after internal approval.
Step 7: Submit shipping bill / invoice proof; assistance released directly to bank account.
eligibility_criteria: Must be APEDA-registered exporter dealing in scheduled products (fruits, vegetables, dairy, meat, processed food, etc.).
Valid RCMC (Registration cum Membership Certificate) from APEDA.
Annual export turnover criteria vary by scheme component.
notes: Different scheme components have different subsidy rates and caps.
Apply within the prescribed timeline post-shipment.
Keep all invoices and shipping documents carefully.
APEDA also provides market intelligence and trade fair participation support.

description: Capital subsidy for dairy farm establishment, milch animal purchase, heifer calf rearing, vermi-composting, and bulk milk cooling units in India.
procedure: Step 1: Prepare a detailed project report (DPR) for the dairy activity.
Step 2: Approach NABARD-approved bank (commercial bank/RRB/cooperative) for term loan.
Step 3: Bank submits loan application with DPR to NABARD for refinance eligibility.
Step 4: NABARD appraises project and issues sanction.
Step 5: Bank disburses loan; borrower implements the project.
Step 6: Upon completion, bank applies to NABARD for capital subsidy release.
Step 7: NABARD verifies utilization and releases back-ended subsidy to bank; bank adjusts in loan account.
eligibility_criteria: Individuals, farmers, NGOs, companies, self-help groups, dairy cooperatives.
Loan availed from NABARD-approved commercial bank, RRB, cooperative bank, or NABARD.
Activities: milk processing, cold chain, dairy farm equipment, transportation.
Subsidy: 25% (general) and 33.33% (SC/ST and NE states) of outlay.
notes: Subsidy is back-ended (released after project completion).
Maximum subsidy: ₹2.50 lakh per unit (general); ₹3.33 lakh (SC/ST/NE).
Apply through bank — not NABARD directly.
Loan repayment typically 5–7 years.

description: Interest reimbursement and capital subsidy for modernisation of textile, handloom, and power loom manufacturing units. Covers spinning, weaving, processing.
procedure: Step 1: Register on TUFS online portal (tufs.gov.in) or approach nearest bank.
Step 2: Identify eligible machinery from TUFS-approved list.
Step 3: Submit loan application to bank along with TUFS application.
Step 4: Bank appraises and sanctions loan; forwards to Ministry of Textiles for TUFS registration.
Step 5: Ministry allocates TUFS unique ID to the unit.
Step 6: Purchase machinery and submit invoices to bank.
Step 7: Interest reimbursement / capital subsidy processed quarterly / annually through bank.
eligibility_criteria: Textile manufacturing MSMEs and large units.
Investment in specified upgraded machinery/technology.
Loan availed from scheduled bank within scheme guidelines.
Eligible segments defined by Ministry of Textiles.
notes: TUFS has had multiple variants (RRTUFS, MTUFS, ATUFS).
Check current active scheme guidelines on Ministry of Textiles website.
Subsidy rate varies by segment (5%–10% capital subsidy or interest reimbursement).

scheme_name: MeitY TIDE 2.0 — Technology Incubation for Entrepreneurs
description: Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs supporting ICT-focused startups through network of 51 incubators with funding and technical mentoring.
procedure: Step 1: Visit MeitY TIDE 2.0 portal (tide.meity.gov.in) and browse empanelled incubators.
Step 2: Apply to relevant incubator with innovation concept note and team profile.
Step 3: Incubator reviews and shortlists applicants for pitch round.
Step 4: Present prototype/concept to incubator selection committee.
Step 5: Selected startups sign incubation agreement; begin receiving mentorship and facilities.
Step 6: Apply for TIDE funding grant through incubator (up to ₹75 lakh for exceptional startups).
Step 7: Submit quarterly progress reports and utilisation certificates.
eligibility_criteria: Technology startup at idea/early stage.
Must apply to TIDE 2.0 supported incubator.
Focus areas: AI/ML, Blockchain, Cybersecurity, IoT, Quantum Computing, Health Tech, Agri-Tech.
Indian incorporated entity.
notes: Grant amount is up to ₹75 lakh for exceptional prototypes; standard is ₹15–25 lakh.
Apply to MeitY-empanelled incubators only — each has specific sector focus.
Milestone-based disbursement.

description: Enhanced capital subsidy for SC/ST entrepreneurs above regular CLCSS. Promotes technology adoption among underrepresented communities.
procedure: Step 1: Register on Udyam Portal and obtain Udyam Registration.
Step 2: Apply on National SC-ST Hub portal (scsthub.in) for enrolment.
Step 3: Identify approved technology from CLCSS eligible list.
Step 4: Approach bank with loan application, DPR, and SC/ST certificate.
Step 5: Bank processes loan and applies for Special CLCSS subsidy through NSSH.
Step 6: NSSH releases 25% capital subsidy to bank.
Step 7: Bank adjusts subsidy against loan principal.
eligibility_criteria: MSME owned and managed by SC/ST entrepreneur (>51% ownership).
Valid Udyam Registration.
Manufacturing sector in eligible sub-sectors.
Term loan from scheduled commercial bank for technology upgrade.
notes: SC/ST Hub offers additional benefits including vendor development, marketing support, and government procurement linkages beyond the special CLCSS.
Caste certificate must be from competent authority in the state.

description: Credit-linked subsidy for setting up new micro enterprises in non-farm sector. Higher subsidy for rural areas, women, SC/ST, ex-servicemen.
procedure: Step 1: Apply online on PMEGP e-Portal (kviconline.gov.in/pmegpeportal).
Step 2: Fill application with personal details, project details, and bank preference.
Step 3: Application forwarded to District Level Task Force Committee (DLTFC) by KVIC/KVIB/DIC.
Step 4: DLTFC reviews applications and shortlists candidates for interview.
Step 5: Attend Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training (10 days mandatory for manufacturing projects above ₹25 lakh).
Step 6: DLTFC recommends application to bank; bank sanctions loan.
Step 7: Project implemented; margin money subsidy released to bank by KVIC on verification.
Step 8: Subsidy held in Fixed Deposit for 3 years; adjusted against loan if repayment on track.
eligibility_criteria: Individual entrepreneurs above 18 years.
For projects above ₹10 lakh (mfg) / ₹5 lakh (service), minimum 8th standard pass.
SHGs, charitable trusts, cooperative societies eligible.
New enterprises only (not existing).
No income ceiling for individuals.
notes: Subsidy: Urban general 15%, Urban SC/ST/Women/Ex-serviceman 25%, Rural general 25%, Rural SC/ST/Women 35%.
Maximum project cost: ₹50 lakh (manufacturing), ₹20 lakh (service).
Second PMEGP loan also available for existing beneficiaries.

scheme_name: SFURTI — Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries
description: Organises traditional industries and artisans into clusters for competitiveness with technology upgradation and sustained employment generation.
procedure: Step 1: Cluster/Nodal Agency identifies a traditional industry cluster with potential.
Step 2: Conduct baseline survey and DPR (Detailed Project Report) for cluster development.
Step 3: Nodal Agency submits application to SFURTI Programme Management Unit (PMU) at KVIC.
Step 4: PMU appraises DPR and conducts field verification.
Step 5: National Level Committee (NLC) approves the cluster project.
Step 6: Funds released to Nodal Agency in tranches for soft and hard interventions.
Step 7: Artisans receive training, equipment, infrastructure, and market linkage support.
documents_required: Land documents for common facility centre
eligibility_criteria: Artisan clusters with minimum 500 artisans (regular clusters) or 1000 artisans (mega clusters).
Implemented through Nodal Agencies (NGOs, industry associations, government bodies).
Individual artisans cannot apply directly — must be part of a cluster.
notes: Individual artisans benefit indirectly through cluster activities.
Government grant covers up to ₹2.5 crore per regular cluster and ₹5 crore for mini clusters.
Contact nearest KVIC/DIC office to identify active SFURTI clusters in your area.

scheme_name: ZED Certification — Zero Defect Zero Effect
description: Promotes quality manufacturing with zero defects and zero environmental effects. Helps MSMEs compete globally. Three levels: Bronze, Silver, Gold.
procedure: Step 1: Register on ZED portal (zed.msme.gov.in) using Udyam Registration Number.
Step 2: Complete self-assessment questionnaire on the portal.
Step 3: Trained ZED assessor visits the unit for initial assessment.
Step 4: Based on assessment score, enterprise is rated: Bronze/Silver/Gold/Diamond.
Step 5: Address gaps and improvement areas identified by assessor.
Step 6: Final certification awarded; subsidy for assessment/certification fees processed by MSME Ministry.
Step 7: Use ZED rating mark in marketing materials and for government procurement preference.
eligibility_criteria: All manufacturing MSMEs with valid Udyam Registration.
Micro units: 80% subsidy on certification fees.
Small units: 60% subsidy.
Medium units: 50% subsidy.
Women/SC/ST enterprises get additional 10% rebate.
notes: ZED certification opens doors to higher government procurement preference.
Bronze level is entry level; Diamond is highest.
Higher ZED rating leads to preference in NSIC Single Point Registration and GeM portal.
Assessment fee is subsidized by government.

description: Online marketplace for government procurement. MSMEs get preferred vendor status, 15% price preference, and EMD exemption for many tenders.
procedure: Step 1: Visit gem.gov.in and click 'Sign Up as Seller'.
Step 2: Select seller category and provide Aadhaar-linked mobile for OTP verification.
Step 3: Fill business details: PAN, Udyam number, GST number, bank account.
Step 4: Upload business documents and complete profile.
Step 5: List products/services with descriptions, images, and pricing.
Step 6: Pass quality/certification check if required for specific product categories.
Step 7: Respond to government buyer tenders and direct purchase orders.
Step 8: Fulfill orders; payment released within 10 days of delivery verification.
eligibility_criteria: Any Indian business entity (sole proprietor, partnership, company, LLP, cooperative) can register.
MSME sellers get purchase preference (25%) and price preference (up to 15% lower price match).
PAN-linked bank account mandatory.
notes: GeM registration is free.
MSMEs must upload Udyam number for purchase preference benefits.
Payments from government buyers are guaranteed and timely.
Dispute resolution mechanism available on the portal.
Turnover not considered for MSME preference.

scheme_name: RAMP — Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance
description: ₹6,000 Crore World Bank-aided scheme enhancing MSME competitiveness through cluster development, market linkage, and technology access.
procedure: Step 1: Check if your state is a RAMP-participating state on msme.gov.in.
Step 2: Identify relevant RAMP sub-component applicable to your business need.
Step 3: Apply through state-level MSME department or Udyam portal for relevant interventions.
Step 4: Participate in RAMP-funded training, technology, or market linkage programmes.
Step 5: Credit access: approach partner financial institutions for RAMP-linked credit products.
Step 6: Submit required documentation as per specific sub-scheme requirements.
Step 7: Track progress and benefits through state MSME portal.
eligibility_criteria: MSMEs registered in participating states.
Various sub-components have different eligibility.
Credit guarantee, technology, and market access sub-components target different MSME segments.
Women-led MSMEs and SC/ST enterprises get priority.
notes: RAMP is a programme framework — specific interventions vary by state.
Check your state's MSME department for RAMP-specific activities.
Focus is on MSMEs facing COVID recovery and competitiveness challenges.

description: 100% guarantee for additional working capital loans to MSMEs. No additional collateral required. Over ₹3.6 Lakh Crore disbursed across versions.
procedure: Step 1: Check eligibility with your existing bank — banks proactively reach out to eligible borrowers.
Step 2: Submit ECLGS application form at your existing lending bank.
Step 3: Bank verifies credit history and outstanding loan amounts.
Step 4: Loan sanctioned: up to 20% of total outstanding credit (additional emergency credit).
Step 5: No fresh collateral required — backed by 100% NCGTC guarantee.
Step 6: Repayment: 4-year tenor with 1 year moratorium on principal.
Step 7: Disbursement into existing loan/current account.
eligibility_criteria: Business entities with total bank credit outstanding ≤₹50 crore as of 29 Feb 2020 (ECLGS 1.0).
Annual turnover ≤₹250 crore.
Not classified as NPA.
GST-registered entities for ECLGS 2.0.
Various expanded versions cover healthcare, hospitality, aviation sectors.
notes: ECLGS has multiple tranches (1.0 to 5.0) with different eligibility.
Primarily accessed through existing lender — not a fresh application process.
Scheme was extended multiple times; check current status. 100% guarantee means no collateral and faster processing.

description: Facilitates bank loans to at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower per bank branch for greenfield enterprise establishment.
procedure: Step 1: Apply online on standupmitra.in or visit nearest bank branch.
Step 2: Select 'Standup India' scheme and fill the application.
Step 3: Provide business plan, project cost estimate, and personal details.
Step 4: Bank registers application on Standup Mitra portal.
Step 5: Handholding agency (LDM/SIDBI) assists in documentation if required.
Step 6: Bank conducts credit assessment and site visit.
Step 7: Loan sanctioned and disbursed; CGTMSE or NCGTC guarantee obtained.
documents_required: Proof of woman ownership (for women applicants)
eligibility_criteria: SC/ST individual borrower or woman borrower above 18 years.
Greenfield (first-time) enterprise in manufacturing, services, or trading sector.
Not a defaulter to any bank.
For non-individual enterprises: majority ownership (>51%) by SC/ST or woman.
notes: Each bank branch is mandated to extend at least one Standup India loan to SC/ST and one to women entrepreneur.
Loan amount: ₹10 lakh–₹1 crore.
Margin contribution: 10–15% by borrower.
Repayment period up to 7 years.

description: Free online MSME registration enabling access to all government schemes, priority sector lending, and procurement preferences. Replaces earlier EM II.
procedure: Step 1: Visit udyamregistration.gov.in.
Step 2: Click 'For New Entrepreneurs who are not Registered as MSME or those with EM-II'.
Step 3: Enter Aadhaar number and validate with OTP sent to Aadhaar-linked mobile.
Step 4: Fill PAN details; system auto-populates ITR data from CBDT.
Step 5: Enter enterprise name, business type, address, NIC code (activity), investment, and turnover.
Step 6: Submit; system generates Udyam Registration Number instantly.
Step 7: Download Udyam Registration Certificate (e-certificate available immediately).
eligibility_criteria: Micro: Investment ≤₹1 crore, Turnover ≤₹5 crore.
Small: Investment ≤₹10 crore, Turnover ≤₹50 crore.
Medium: Investment ≤₹50 crore, Turnover ≤₹250 crore.
Both manufacturing and service enterprises eligible.
notes: Udyam registration is FREE — no fees involved.
Registration is self-declared (no inspection or certification needed).
Certificate is auto-generated instantly.
Existing EM-II and Udyog Aadhaar holders must migrate to Udyam.
Single registration sufficient for all MSME benefits.

description: ₹10,683 Crore PLI for Man-Made Fibre apparel, MMF fabrics, and technical textile products. 10-year incentive period for global competitiveness.
procedure: Step 1: Check eligibility and product line coverage in Ministry of Textiles PLI guidelines.
Step 2: Register company on PLI Textiles portal (plitextiles.gov.in).
Step 3: Submit application with investment plan, base year turnover, and financial projections.
Step 4: Application evaluated by Ministry of Textiles; site inspection conducted.
Step 5: Approval letter issued with incentive conditions.
Step 6: Make required investments in approved facilities and machinery.
Step 7: Submit annual sales and production data; Ministry releases incentive based on incremental sales.
eligibility_criteria: Existing manufacturers with minimum ₹100 crore investment (MMF) or ₹50 crore (technical textiles).
Fresh investments in eligible product lines.
MSMEs with ₹10 crore minimum for technical textiles segment. 5-year incentive period.
Registered company in India.
notes: PLI scheme applications open in specific tranches — check Ministry of Textiles website for open windows.
Incentive is on incremental sales above base year. 5-year incentive period.
Annual reporting mandatory.

description: ₹10,900 Crore PLI for innovative and organic products, mozzarella cheese, and ready-to-eat food segments targeting ₹33,494 Crore exports.
procedure: Step 1: Check Ministry of Food Processing Industries PLI guidelines and eligible product list.
Step 2: Register on MoFPI PLI portal and create applicant profile.
Step 3: Submit detailed application with investment plan, product details, and base year turnover.
Step 4: Application reviewed by Project Management Agency (PMA).
Step 5: Inspection and verification of manufacturing facility.
Step 6: Approval issued with eligible product lines confirmed.
Step 7: Submit annual sales data; PLI incentive released after verification.
eligibility_criteria: Companies/MSMEs in food processing segment.
SME category: sales ₹5–75 crore.
Large category: sales ₹75 crore and above.
Investment commitment required.
Products in four segments: ready-to-cook/eat, processed fruits & vegetables, marine products, innovative food products.
notes: PLI incentive: 10% on incremental sales in years 1–2; 9% in year 3; reducing thereafter. 6-year incentive period.
FSSAI compliance mandatory.
SME segment has lower investment threshold.

description: ₹15,000 Crore PLI for critical APIs, complex generics, biopharmaceuticals, and patented drugs to reduce import dependence.
procedure: Step 1: Identify applicable category under PLI Pharma scheme.
Step 2: Register on PLI portal for pharmaceuticals (pli.gov.in or through DPIIT).
Step 3: Submit application with investment details and base year sales data.
Step 4: Application reviewed by Pharma Department/DPIIT.
Step 5: Approval issued; commence qualifying sales.
Step 6: Annual submission of sales/production data with CA certification.
Step 7: PLI released on incremental sales above base year.
eligibility_criteria: Registered Indian pharmaceutical company.
Category 1 (new producers of KSM/drug intermediates/APIs), Category 2 (biopharmaceuticals), Category 3 (repurposed drugs, autoimmune drugs, anti-cancer).
Minimum investment thresholds per category.
Valid drug manufacturing licence.
notes: 6-year incentive period.
Incentive rate varies by category (3%–10%).
GMP compliance mandatory.
Annual inspection by CDSCO.
Quarterly sales data submission required.

description: ₹7,350 Crore PLI for mobile phones, laptops, tablets, and IT hardware manufacturing. 16 companies approved including global players.
procedure: Step 1: Review MeitY PLI-IT Hardware scheme guidelines.
Step 2: Apply on MeitY portal (meity.gov.in/esdm) during open application window.
Step 3: Submit business plan, investment commitment, and product specifications.
Step 4: MeitY evaluation committee reviews applications.
Step 5: Approval letter issued with conditions.
Step 6: Set up manufacturing; commence production and sales.
Step 7: Submit sales data; claim PLI incentive annually.
eligibility_criteria: Global or Indian electronics manufacturer.
Minimum turnover thresholds apply per category.
Products: laptops, tablets, all-in-one PCs, servers, IoT devices.
Investment commitment of ₹100 crore+ (large category) or ₹5 crore (emerging category).
notes: PLI incentive is 1%–4% on incremental domestic sales. 5-year incentive period.
Companies must sell eligible products in domestic market.
Global companies must have India-registered entity.

scheme_name: DST-NIDHI — National Initiative Developing & Harnessing Innovations
description: Comprehensive programme for innovation and entrepreneurship through 130+ incubator funding, startup grants, and accelerator support across India.
procedure: Step 1: Identify relevant NIDHI component (Prayas, SSS, Accelerator, EIR).
Step 2: Apply through DST NIDHI portal (nidhi.dst.gov.in) or through empanelled incubators.
Step 3: Submit innovation concept, prototyping plan, and team details.
Step 4: NIDHI Prayas: apply at Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) affiliated with DST.
Step 5: Selection committee evaluates technical and commercial feasibility.
Step 6: Grant agreement signed; milestone-based funding disbursed.
Step 7: Submit periodic technical and utilization reports.
eligibility_criteria: Innovators from universities, IITs, NITs, research labs, or independent innovators.
NIDHI Prayas: ₹10 lakh grant for prototyping.
NIDHI SSS: Startup support ₹50 lakh.
NIDHI Accelerator: growth-stage startups.
DPIIT recognition preferred.
notes: NIDHI Prayas: up to ₹10 lakh for prototyping; NIDHI SSS: up to ₹50 lakh for commercialization.
Funding is via empanelled TBIs — apply to TBI, not DST directly.
Academic innovators can apply without company registration.

description: Early-stage grant for biotech startups translating academic research into product concepts. Managed through 40+ BIRAC partner incubators.
procedure: Step 1: Visit BIRAC portal (birac.nic.in) and check open BIG call for proposals.
Step 2: Register on BIRAC portal and complete applicant profile.
Step 3: Submit detailed proposal including technology description, proof of concept plan, team profile, and budget.
Step 4: BIG scientific committee reviews proposals; shortlisted applicants invited for presentation.
Step 5: Present technology concept to expert committee.
Step 6: Grant agreement signed with BIRAC on approval.
Step 7: Funding released in tranches; submit quarterly technical and financial progress reports.
eligibility_criteria: Indian citizens/institutions at idea/early innovation stage.
Both individual innovators and small companies eligible.
Technology must be in biology/life sciences/biotech/healthcare.
Innovation must address unmet need with novelty.
notes: BIG grant is up to ₹50 lakh for 18 months.
Competition is high — success rate ~15–20%.
Calls are periodic (2–3 times a year).
IP generated belongs to grantee with BIRAC march-in rights.

scheme_name: BIRAC BIPP — Biotechnology Industry Partnership Programme
description: Funds industry-driven collaborative R&D in biotechnology with high societal impact. Industry-academia collaboration mandatory.
procedure: Step 1: Form consortium between industry partner and research institution.
Step 2: Develop joint research proposal with defined milestones.
Step 3: Submit proposal on BIRAC BIPP portal during open call.
Step 4: Scientific and technical review by BIRAC expert committee.
Step 5: Due diligence on company financials and research plan.
Step 6: Grant agreement executed with both consortium partners.
Step 7: Funds released milestone-wise with quarterly reporting.
documents_required: Consortium agreement between industry and institution
eligibility_criteria: Indian biotech/pharma company (MSME or large) in consortium with reputed research institution.
Joint project on innovative biotech product.
Company must commit matching funds.
SEBI-registered AIF or equivalent financial backing preferred.
notes: BIPP requires at least 50% industry funding contribution.
Maximum grant ₹5 crore for 3 years.
IP sharing must be pre-agreed.
BIRAC retains march-in rights for public health purposes.

description: Sets up Technology and Livelihood Business Incubators at ITIs and agriculture science centres for rural entrepreneurs in non-farm sector.
procedure: Step 1: Identify ASPIRE-approved Livelihood Business Incubator (LBI) in your district via KVIC website.
Step 2: Apply to the LBI with business idea and personal background.
Step 3: Attend entrepreneurship development training at LBI.
Step 4: Develop business plan with LBI support.
Step 5: Apply for credit linkage through LBI-partnered banks.
Step 6: Avail incubation support: mentoring, market linkage, raw material access.
Step 7: Graduate from incubation with functional enterprise and bank credit.
eligibility_criteria: Rural entrepreneurs, agri-business innovators, artisans, and SHG members.
Must be associated with an ASPIRE-approved LBI.
Focus on agri, food processing, rural manufacturing, handicrafts.
No specific income bar.
notes: ASPIRE is implemented through LBIs — find the nearest LBI through KVIC or MSME district office.
Incubation period is typically 12–18 months.
Credit linkage via MUDRA or PMEGP available through LBI.

description: Recognition and support for 18 traditional trades including carpenter, goldsmith, tailor, blacksmith, potter. Includes ₹5L credit, skill training, digital tools.
procedure: Step 1: Visit nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or apply on pmvishwakarma.gov.in.
Step 2: Complete biometric verification (Aadhaar authentication) at CSC.
Step 3: Register as artisan and select craft/trade category.
Step 4: Participate in basic training (5 days) and advanced training (15 days) at designated training centre.
Step 5: Receive PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card post-training.
Step 6: Apply for Toolkit Grant (₹15,000) through portal.
Step 7: Apply for Vishwakarma Credit (₹1 lakh collateral-free at 5% interest); second loan ₹2 lakh after repayment.
Step 8: Onboard to digital payment systems; earn ₹1/transaction incentive.
documents_required: Aadhaar of family members (to check family eligibility)
eligibility_criteria: Must belong to one of 18 traditional artisan communities (Kumbhar, Lohar, Sunar, Darzi, Mochidar, Nai, Dhobhi, Malakaar, etc.).
Age 18+.
Must be self-employed.
Not availed PMEGP/MUDRA/Standup India in last 5 years.
Family member already enrolled in PM Vishwakarma is ineligible.
notes: Application must be done at CSC with biometric verification.
Training is mandatory before credit/toolkit.
Digital payment incentive: ₹1 per transaction up to 100 transactions/month. 18 trades covered — verify your craft is listed.

scheme_name: PM SVANidhi — Street Vendor Micro-Credit Scheme
description: Micro-credit facility for street vendors to restart livelihoods. Enhanced credit limits on regular repayment. Digital payment incentive of ₹1,200/year.
procedure: Step 1: Contact Urban Local Body (ULB) / Municipality to obtain Certificate of Vending or LoR.
Step 2: Apply online at pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in or via CSC, bank branches, or MFIs.
Step 3: Submit application with ULB certificate and KYC documents.
Step 4: Bank/MFI processes application and sanctions ₹10,000 (first loan).
Step 5: Receive loan; make regular repayments over 12 months.
Step 6: On timely repayment, apply for enhanced loan (₹20,000 in second cycle; ₹50,000 in third).
Step 7: Use UPI/digital payments and earn up to ₹1,200/year cashback incentive.
documents_required: Certificate of Vending or Letter of Recommendation from ULB
eligibility_criteria: Street vendors operating in urban areas as of 24 March 2020.
Must have Certificate of Vending (CoV) or Letter of Recommendation (LoR) from Urban Local Body (ULB).
Rural vendors in peri-urban areas also covered under extended guidelines.
notes: Digital payment incentive: ₹50/month for 100+ digital transactions.
Loan is at 7% annual interest with subsidy.
Credit limit increases with timely repayment — ₹10k → ₹20k → ₹50k.
ULB registration as vendor is the first mandatory step.

description: Financial assistance for purchase of raw material (indigenous and imported) to overcome working capital shortage. Benefit of bulk purchase pricing.
procedure: Step 1: Register for NSIC Single Point Registration at nsic.co.in.
Step 2: Apply for Raw Material Assistance with business financial details.
Step 3: NSIC conducts credit assessment and sets credit limit.
Step 4: NSIC empanelled supplier supplies raw material to MSME on credit.
Step 5: MSME repays NSIC within 90–180 days as per credit terms.
Step 6: NSIC provides bank guarantee to supplier on behalf of MSME.
Step 7: Annual renewal of credit limit based on utilization and repayment.
documents_required: Audited Balance Sheet and P&L (3 years)
eligibility_criteria: Manufacturing MSME with Udyam Registration.
Must register with NSIC (Single Point Registration).
Satisfactory credit track record.
Not an NPA with any bank.
Annual credit limit set by NSIC based on financial assessment.
notes: NSIC charges a service charge (typically 1.25%–1.75% p.a.).
Credit limit ranges from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 crore.
Helps MSMEs avoid upfront raw material payment.
NSIC provides bank guarantee to suppliers.

description: Provides bee boxes, bee colonies, and free training to rural entrepreneurs, tribals, and women for honey production and value addition.
procedure: Step 1: Apply at nearest KVIC District Office or Khadi institution.
Step 2: Fill application form specifying number of bee boxes required.
Step 3: Attend beekeeping training (5–7 days) at KVIC training centre.
Step 4: KVIC verifies application and processes subsidy.
Step 5: Bee boxes and colonies supplied at subsidized or free cost.
Step 6: KVIC provides handholding and market linkage support.
Step 7: Link to KVIC's honey procurement and NAFED for market access.
documents_required: Land ownership proof or farmer ID
eligibility_criteria: Rural unemployed youth and farmers.
Age 18–50 years.
Preference: SC/ST, women, and tribal communities.
Must attend beekeeping training.
Income limit: BPL or marginal farmer preferred.
No prior beekeeping experience needed.
notes: Honey Mission provides free bee boxes under KVIC's National Beekeeping and Honey Mission.
Each box can generate income of ₹10,000–₹15,000/year.
KVIC provides buyback for honey produced.
Contact nearest KVIC office as allocation is on first-come basis.

description: Introduces lean manufacturing concepts to MSMEs via Light Engineering Cluster programme. Reduces waste, improves productivity and quality.
procedure: Step 1: Form a mini-cluster of 10+ MSMEs in same sector/geography.
Step 2: Apply on MSME Lean portal or through nearest MSME-DI/DIC office.
Step 3: Application reviewed; cluster approved by MSME Ministry.
Step 4: Government empanelled Lean Manufacturing Consultant (LMC) assigned to cluster.
Step 5: LMC conducts 18-month lean implementation programme across all cluster units.
Step 6: Pay 20% of consultant fee (government pays 80%).
Step 7: Receive lean certification and performance improvement documentation.
documents_required: Udyam Registration of all cluster members
eligibility_criteria: Manufacturing MSMEs forming a mini-cluster of minimum 10 enterprises.
Willing to implement lean manufacturing, 5S, and waste reduction.
Udyam registered.
Cluster typically in same geography/sector.
notes: Government bears 80% consultant cost; enterprise pays 20%.
Lean implementation covers 5S, Value Stream Mapping, TPM, Kaizen.
Post-implementation, enterprises see 20–40% productivity improvement.
MSME clusters in same sector/geography are easier to form.

scheme_name: DST SEED — Science for Equity Empowerment & Development
description: Funds S&T interventions for socioeconomic development of disadvantaged communities in rural areas through applied science.
procedure: Step 1: Visit DST SEED Division portal (dst.gov.in/seed-division).
Step 2: Identify relevant SEED programme: SYST (Science for Youth), MANAK, or Grassroots Innovation.
Step 3: Submit project proposal with technical details, social impact, and budget.
Step 4: Review by SEED advisory committee.
Step 5: Field verification of innovator/institution.
Step 6: Grant agreement and disbursement in tranches.
Step 7: Submit quarterly reports and field demonstration.
eligibility_criteria: Scientists/researchers/NGOs working on solutions for disadvantaged groups.
Projects must have direct livelihood or social impact.
Individual innovators from rural/tribal communities.
No minimum educational qualification for grassroots innovations.
notes: SEED grants range from ₹5 lakh to ₹50 lakh.
Focus on technologies for rural livelihood, water, energy, health, and agriculture.
Calls for proposals issued periodically.
Social enterprises and NGOs also eligible.

scheme_name: EXIM Bank Lending Programme for Exporters
description: Pre-shipment and post-shipment credit for MSME exporters. Buyer's credit and government-to-government lines of credit for Indian goods.
procedure: Step 1: Contact nearest EXIM Bank branch or apply online at eximbankindia.in.
Step 2: Submit export credit application with export order/L/C details.
Step 3: EXIM Bank assesses creditworthiness and export transaction.
Step 4: Sanction letter issued for appropriate credit facility.
Step 5: Disburse pre-shipment credit for production/procurement.
Step 6: Post-shipment: submit shipping documents; convert to export bill discounting.
Step 7: Repayment from export proceeds received.
eligibility_criteria: Indian exporter with IEC and valid export orders/L/C.
Both MSME and large exporters eligible.
Various products: PCFC (Pre-shipment Credit in Foreign Currency), EPC, post-shipment credit, project export finance.
notes: EXIM Bank interest rates are competitive (linked to SOFR/LIBOR or MCLR).
Pre-shipment credit available in INR and foreign currency.
Also provides lines of credit to foreign governments for Indian export.
MSME exporters get priority under NeSL e-discounting.

description: Capital investment subsidy for cold storage, pack-houses, CA stores, and primary processing centres for horticulture products.
procedure: Step 1: Prepare project report for horticulture infrastructure.
Step 2: Approach scheduled commercial bank or NABARD for term loan.
Step 3: Bank appraises project and forwards to NHB for subsidy registration.
Step 4: NHB registers the project and issues provisional approval.
Step 5: Implement project (construction, equipment installation).
Step 6: NHB inspection post-completion.
Step 7: Capital subsidy released by NHB to bank; adjusted against loan.
eligibility_criteria: Individual farmers, farmer groups, FPOs, companies, cooperatives.
Investment in horticulture infrastructure (cold storage, CA storage, packhouses, tissue culture labs, processing).
Loan from scheduled bank/NHB.
notes: Capital subsidy: 25% for general; 33.33% for SC/ST/NE states.
Maximum subsidy ₹20–₹56 lakh per project depending on type.
NHB also provides direct loans for nursery development.

description: ₹4,600 Crore scheme for modern food processing infrastructure — mega food parks, cold chain, and backward-forward linkages. Reduces post-harvest losses.
procedure: Step 1: Identify relevant PMKSY sub-scheme (Mega Food Park, Cold Chain, APC, or Creation of Processing Capacity).
Step 2: Apply on MoFPI portal (mofpi.gov.in) during open application window.
Step 3: Submit Detailed Project Report (DPR) with financial plan.
Step 4: Technical and financial appraisal by MoFPI/empanelled agency.
Step 5: Approval letter issued with grant amount and conditions.
Step 6: Implement project and submit utilization certificates.
Step 7: Grant released in tranches against verified milestones.
eligibility_criteria: Companies, cooperatives, FPOs, SHGs in food processing sector.
Various sub-schemes have different eligibility: Agro-Processing Cluster (APC): SPV of 50+ units; Cold Chain: individual companies.
FSSAI licence required.
NE states get higher subsidy.
notes: Grant varies by sub-scheme: Cold Chain up to ₹10 crore; Mega Food Park up to ₹50 crore.
Applications accepted in specific rounds/windows.
NE & hilly states get 33% higher subsidy.
FSSAI compliance is mandatory.

scheme_name: PM Formalization of Micro Food Enterprises (PMFME)
description: ₹10,000 Crore scheme for formalization and upgrade of 2 Lakh micro food enterprises. Includes branding, packaging, and FPO support.
procedure: Step 1: Register on PMFME portal (pmfme.mofpi.gov.in).
Step 2: Select ODOP (One District One Product) category for your district or any food product.
Step 3: Apply for credit-linked subsidy with bank loan application.
Step 4: Bank processes loan (typically ₹10 lakh–₹30 lakh); government provides 35% subsidy.
Step 5: Obtain FSSAI Basic Registration/State Licence (support provided free).
Step 6: Attend skill training as scheduled by MoFPI/state nodal agency.
Step 7: Avail branding, packaging, and marketing support from the scheme.
eligibility_criteria: Existing micro food enterprise (informal unit) with annual turnover up to ₹5 lakh.
Individual/proprietary micro FPE.
One unit per family.
Must obtain FSSAI licence.
SHGs, FPOs, cooperatives also eligible for enhanced support.
notes: 35% capital subsidy capped at ₹10 lakh per unit.
One unit per family eligible.
FSSAI registration support is free.
ODOP product is preferred (check your district's ODOP).
SHGs get additional working capital support.

description: KVIC-specific channel for PMEGP exclusively for traditional village and khadi industries with slightly different implementing guidelines.
procedure: Step 1: Apply on PMEGP e-portal (kviconline.gov.in/pmegpeportal) and select KVIC as implementing agency.
Step 2: Fill application with details of proposed khadi/village industry project.
Step 3: Application forwarded to nearest KVIC district office for scrutiny.
Step 4: Attend interview before DLTFC (District Level Task Force Committee).
Step 5: Complete mandatory EDP (Entrepreneurship Development Programme) training.
Step 6: Bank sanctions loan; KVIC releases margin money subsidy.
Step 7: Subsidy locked in FD for 3 years; adjusted if repayment is regular.
eligibility_criteria: Individual above 18 years applying via KVIC route.
Project in rural area or khadi/village industry. 8th standard pass for projects above ₹10 lakh.
No income ceiling.
SHGs and cooperatives also eligible via KVIC.
notes: KVIC channel is suitable for village/cottage/khadi industries.
Subsidy rates same as PMEGP general: 25% urban, 35% rural for special categories.
Prefer KVIC channel if your activity is khadi/handloom/village industry related.

scheme_name: Standup India — Stand Up Mitra Portal
description: Online handholding portal for SC/ST and women Standup India borrowers. Connects with banks, incubators, training partners, and government schemes.
procedure: Step 1: Visit standupmitra.in and register as applicant.
Step 2: Complete online application with personal, business, and loan details.
Step 3: Portal connects applicant with nearest Lead District Manager (LDM) or bank.
Step 4: Handholding agencies (SIDCOs, NSIC, etc.) assist with documentation if required.
Step 5: Bank receives application from portal and initiates processing.
Step 6: Credit appraisal; site visit; loan sanctioned.
Step 7: Disbursement; CGTMSE or NCGTC guarantee arranged.
eligibility_criteria: SC/ST individual or woman above 18 years seeking greenfield enterprise loan of ₹10 lakh–₹1 crore.
Not a defaulter.
Business in manufacturing, services, or trading.
Majority SC/ST/women ownership.
notes: Standup Mitra portal provides online application tracking and handholding.
Each bank branch mandated to give one loan each to SC/ST and women entrepreneur.
Repayment up to 7 years with moratorium.

scheme_name: IPR Scheme — Patent & Trademark Fee Rebate for MSMEs
description: 80% fee rebate for MSMEs and startups filing patents, trademarks, and industrial designs. Encourages IP creation and protection.
procedure: Step 1: Register on IP India portal (ipindia.gov.in) for patents/trademarks.
Step 2: For patent: file Form 1 (application) and Form 2 (specification) online.
Step 3: Upload Udyam certificate to avail 80% fee rebate — enter Udyam number in application.
Step 4: For trademark: file Form TM-A online; select MSME category for 50% fee reduction.
Step 5: Pay reduced fees as applicable (patent: ₹1,600 instead of ₹8,000 for micro/small).
Step 6: Application published in IP India journal; examination begins.
Step 7: Respond to examination queries; receive grant/registration certificate.
eligibility_criteria: All MSMEs with Udyam Registration. 80% rebate on patent filing fees (for startup recognized by DPIIT: 80%). 50% rebate on trademark registration fees.
Design registration also covered.
Both individuals and MSME entities eligible.
notes: File patents early — priority date matters.
Patent process takes 3–5 years; trademark typically 18–24 months.
Consider filing provisional specification first to establish priority.
Free IP facilitation centres at MSME Technology Centres.

scheme_name: Startup India Tax Exemption under Section 80-IAC
description: DPIIT-recognised startups get 100% income tax exemption for any 3 consecutive assessment years within first 10 years. Apply through IMB.
procedure: Step 1: Obtain DPIIT recognition certificate from startupindia.gov.in.
Step 2: Apply for Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) on Startup India portal under 80-IAC section.
Step 3: Fill Form 1 (Application for Certificate) with business details and innovation description.
Step 4: Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) of DPIIT evaluates startup for innovation and scalability.
Step 5: CoE issued if startup is approved as eligible under Section 80-IAC.
Step 6: File Income Tax return claiming 80-IAC deduction for relevant assessment years.
Step 7: Maintain proper books and audited accounts for tax department scrutiny.
eligibility_criteria: Must be DPIIT-recognised startup.
Incorporated as Pvt Ltd company or LLP.
Annual turnover ≤₹100 crore in all years since incorporation.
Engaged in eligible business (innovation/scalable model).
Apply to DPIIT for Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) before filing ITR.
notes: Tax holiday is for 3 consecutive years of profit — choose the most profitable years.
Turnover must not exceed ₹100 crore.
Apply for CoE before the end of financial year for which exemption is claimed.
MAT (Minimum Alternate Tax) still applies.

description: DPIIT-recognised startups exempted from angel tax on investments received from resident investors above fair market value. Key barrier removed.
procedure: Step 1: Ensure startup has valid DPIIT recognition certificate.
Step 2: After receiving angel investment, file 'Form 2' on Startup India portal within 3 months of investment.
Step 3: Declaration that paid-up capital + premium does not exceed ₹25 crore.
Step 4: Startup receives DPIIT acknowledgment of Form 2 filing.
Step 5: Mention exemption in ITR filing; keep Form 2 acknowledgment as proof.
Step 6: If IT department raises query, submit DPIIT Form 2 acknowledgment.
documents_required: Valuation report from SEBI-registered merchant banker
eligibility_criteria: DPIIT-recognised startup.
Aggregate paid-up share capital + share premium after investment does not exceed ₹25 crore.
Must file Form 2 with DPIIT.
Investor must be a non-specified entity (not VC/AIF — those already exempt).
notes: Angel tax exemption is up to ₹25 crore total investment.
For investments from SEBI-registered Category I AIFs, angel tax does not apply regardless.
Get a Section 56 compliant valuation (DCF method) from registered merchant banker before issuing shares.

scheme_name: RuPay Credit Card for MSMEs on UPI
description: Credit card on UPI platform for MSME owners enabling digital working capital access. Linked to Udyam registration for instant credit access.
procedure: Step 1: Contact your existing bank (PSU or private) for RuPay MSME Credit Card.
Step 2: Submit Udyam Registration and KYC documents.
Step 3: Bank assesses credit limit based on business financials.
Step 4: Credit card issued and linked to UPI app (PhonePe/BHIM/GPay supporting RuPay credit).
Step 5: Use card for business purchases at UPI QR merchants.
Step 6: Repay monthly statement with interest-free period (typically 45–50 days).
Step 7: Avail cash management features through bank portal.
eligibility_criteria: Udyam-registered MSME with existing banking relationship.
Credit limit set by issuing bank based on MSME creditworthiness.
Business account holder with satisfactory track record.
notes: Multiple banks (SBI, BOB, Union Bank) now offer RuPay MSME credit cards.
Credit limits typically ₹50,000–₹10 lakh.
Key benefit: use credit line at any UPI QR-accepting merchant without swipe machine.

description: Single Point Registration enables MSMEs to participate in government tenders without Earnest Money Deposit and with 15% price preference over large firms.
procedure: Step 1: Visit nsic.co.in and apply for Single Point Registration online or at nearest NSIC branch.
Step 2: Submit application form with business profile, product/service list.
Step 3: NSIC assesses plant and machinery (for manufacturing) or service capabilities.
Step 4: Pay registration fee (based on turnover slab).
Step 5: NSIC conducts physical inspection of premises.
Step 6: Registration certificate issued listing products/services and monetary limit.
Step 7: Quote in government tenders using NSIC registration; claim EMD waiver.
eligibility_criteria: Manufacturing or service MSME with Udyam Registration.
Valid product/service to supply to government.
Quality certification (BIS/ISO) preferred.
Registration valid for 2 years; renewal required.
notes: NSIC-registered MSMEs get EMD exemption in government tenders. 25% purchase preference in central government procurement.
Monetary limit set based on last 2 years average annual turnover.
Registration fee ranges ₹3,000–₹10,000 based on size.

description: Concessional finance to minority communities (Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Parsi, Jain) for self-employment and income-generating activities.
procedure: Step 1: Approach State Channelizing Agency (SCA) — state minorities corporation — in your state.
Step 2: Obtain application form from SCA or download from nmdfc.org.
Step 3: Submit application with income proof, project proposal, and community certificate.
Step 4: SCA evaluates and forwards to NMDFC.
Step 5: NMDFC sanctions loan; SCA disburses to beneficiary.
Step 6: Repay to SCA in quarterly/monthly installments over agreed period.
Step 7: Maintain loan account with SCA.
eligibility_criteria: Belong to minority community (Muslim/Christian/Sikh/Buddhist/Parsi/Jain).
Annual family income ≤₹1.5 lakh (rural) or ≤₹2 lakh (urban).
Age 18–55 years.
Must not have availed similar government scheme benefit.
Viable income-generating proposal.
notes: Apply through State Channelizing Agency (different for each state — e.g., TAMILNADU Wakf Board, Maharashtra Minorities Finance Corp).
Interest rate: 6% p.a. (women: 5%).
Repayment period up to 5 years.
Maximum loan: ₹30 lakh.

scheme_name: PM PMKVY 4.0 — Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana
description: Flagship skill development scheme with 300+ job roles. NSDC-accredited training with assessment and certification. Target 1.4 Crore youth by 2026.
procedure: Step 1: Visit skillindiadigital.gov.in or pmkvyofficial.org and register.
Step 2: Search for training centre near your location and preferred skill/sector.
Step 3: Enroll at PMKVY-empanelled Training Centre (TC) with Aadhaar.
Step 4: Attend free training as per course curriculum (typically 100–300 hours).
Step 5: Appear for assessment by SSC (Sector Skill Council).
Step 6: Receive QP-NOS based certification on pass.
Step 7: Access placement support through Training Centre and NSDC.
eligibility_criteria: Indian citizen aged 15–45 years.
No minimum education for most courses.
Special focus on school/college dropouts.
Industry 4.0 courses target graduates.
Aadhaar mandatory for enrollment.
notes: Training is completely free.
Post-assessment incentive/reward for passing.
PMKVY 4.0 focuses on Industry 4.0, drone, AI, and green jobs.
Salary/stipend support available.
Find nearest training centre at skillindiadigital.gov.in.

description: Special credit card for PM Vishwakarma artisans at concessional 5% interest rate. First tranche ₹1 Lakh, second tranche ₹2 Lakh.
procedure: Step 1: First enroll in PM Vishwakarma scheme at CSC or pmvishwakarma.gov.in.
Step 2: Complete basic (5-day) and advanced (15-day) training.
Step 3: Apply for Vishwakarma Credit Card through designated bank (linked to PM Vishwakarma portal).
Step 4: Bank issues ₹1 lakh credit at 5% per annum (interest subsidy by government).
Step 5: Repay ₹1 lakh loan; apply for second tranche of ₹2 lakh.
Step 6: Use credit for raw material, tools, working capital.
Step 7: Digital payment adoption earns additional ₹1/transaction incentive.
documents_required: PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card
eligibility_criteria: Must be registered under PM Vishwakarma scheme.
Must have completed basic skill training.
Good repayment track record on first credit for second tranche.
Belongs to 18 eligible traditional crafts/trades.
notes: Interest rate is 5% p.a. (government subsidizes the difference with market rate).
First loan ₹1 lakh; second ₹2 lakh on timely repayment.
Repayment period: 18 months.
Toolkit grant (₹15,000) received before credit application.

scheme_name: Udyam Assist Platform — Informal MSME Formalisation
description: Enables informal micro enterprises without GST/ITR to get Udyam Assist Certificate for MSME scheme benefits. Especially for KCC-linked artisans.
procedure: Step 1: Visit udyamassist.gov.in — available only through assisted mode (CSC, bank, MFI).
Step 2: Approach nearest CSC/Jan Seva Kendra/bank/MFI branch.
Step 3: Provide Aadhaar for biometric authentication.
Step 4: Provide basic business details (name, activity, bank account).
Step 5: Platform generates Udyam Assist Certificate for informal micro enterprise.
Step 6: Use certificate to access MUDRA loans, PM SVANidhi, and other micro-enterprise schemes.
Step 7: Work towards formal Udyam Registration as business grows.
documents_required: Basic business activity proof (bank statement or self-declaration)
eligibility_criteria: Micro enterprises in informal sector.
Do not have GST registration or ITR.
Can provide bank statement or Aadhaar-linked business activity proof.
Includes small traders, artisans, service providers without formal registration.
notes: Udyam Assist is for informal enterprises only — formal enterprises should use Udyam Registration.
Must be accessed through assisted mode (CSC/bank).
Certificate is provisional and differs from Udyam Registration.
Helps bridge the formal-informal gap.

description: Portal for MSMEs to file applications against buyers for delayed payments beyond 45 days under MSMED Act 2006. MSEFC adjudication within 90 days.
procedure: Step 1: Visit samadhaan.msme.gov.in and login with Udyam credentials.
Step 2: File online application with details of buyer, invoice amount, and delay period.
Step 3: Upload invoices, purchase orders, and delivery proofs.
Step 4: Application forwarded to MSEFC of respective state.
Step 5: MSEFC issues notice to buyer; buyer required to respond.
Step 6: Conciliation process between buyer and MSME (up to 90 days).
Step 7: If unresolved, MSEFC issues award with principal + compound interest (RBI rate x 3) to MSME.
eligibility_criteria: Any MSME with Udyam Registration.
Payment delayed beyond 45 days by buyer.
Buyer can be private company, government department, or PSU.
Written agreement or purchase order establishing supply must exist.
notes: Interest on delayed payment is compound interest at 3 times RBI bank rate — very penal for the buyer.
MSEFC orders are enforceable as court decree.
Government departments must pay within 45 days as per MSMED Act 2006.
File within limitation period.

scheme_name: SIDBI SMILE — Soft Loan for Micro and Small Enterprises
description: Quasi-equity soft loans to MSMEs for capacity expansion and modernisation at below-market interest rates. Flexible repayment structure.
procedure: Step 1: Apply on SIDBI portal (sidbi.in) or approach nearest SIDBI branch.
Step 2: Submit application with project details and primary loan sanction letter from bank.
Step 3: SIDBI appraises project — focuses on promoter quality and business viability.
Step 4: SMILE sanction letter issued; loan agreement executed.
Step 5: SIDBI disburses soft loan directly to enterprise bank account.
Step 6: Repay over 10 years (with 3-year moratorium on principal).
Step 7: Track repayment; prepayment allowed without penalty.
documents_required: Audited financials (2 years) or projections for new enterprise
eligibility_criteria: Micro and small manufacturing enterprises.
Udyam registered.
Both greenfield and brownfield projects.
Borrower should have taken or be taking term loan from bank/other FI.
SIDBI SMILE acts as supplementary soft loan.
notes: SMILE is soft loan at 8–9% p.a. — lower than market rates.
Maximum ₹25 lakh. 10-year repayment with 3-year grace period.
No collateral required below ₹10 lakh (covered by CGTMSE).
Ideal as top-up financing for undercapitalized MSMEs.

scheme_name: SIDBI Make in India MSME Loan — 59-Minute Approval
description: In-Principle approval within 59 minutes for MSME loans up to ₹5 Crore. Integration with GST, ITR, and bank statement data for instant assessment.
procedure: Step 1: Visit psbloansin59minutes.com and register with PAN and Aadhaar.
Step 2: Provide GST credentials, IT return data, and bank statement (auto-fetched via API).
Step 3: Specify loan amount and purpose (term loan or working capital).
Step 4: Select preferred bank from list of partner PSU banks.
Step 5: Receive in-principle approval within 59 minutes (system-generated).
Step 6: Visit selected bank branch with original documents for final processing.
Step 7: Bank completes KYC, site visit, and disburses loan.
documents_required: Net Banking Credentials (for bank statement auto-fetch)
eligibility_criteria: GST-registered MSME with minimum 6 months of GST returns.
Active bank account with 6 months statements.
Udyam registered.
No NPA.
ITR for last 2 years.
notes: 59 minutes is for in-principle approval — actual disbursement takes 7–14 days after branch visit.
Available for loans up to ₹5 crore.
CGTMSE and MUDRA collateral-free options available on this portal.

description: Comprehensive development for handloom weavers — technology, design, raw material supply, and market development. 35 Lakh weavers covered.
procedure: Step 1: Register as handloom weaver with state handloom department and obtain weaver identity card.
Step 2: Apply for relevant component: yarn supply at subsidised rate, design grant, or cluster support.
Step 3: Approach state handloom corporation or NHDC (National Handloom Development Corp) for yarn subsidy.
Step 4: Submit weaver identity card and bank details for direct benefit transfer.
Step 5: For cluster development, DIC/state handloom dept facilitates cluster application.
Step 6: Marketing support: apply for India Handloom Brand certification through state handloom dept.
Step 7: Receive subsidy, training, and market linkage as per approved component.
eligibility_criteria: Handloom weavers with Bunkar Mitra/weaver's identity card.
Weaver cooperatives and SHGs in handloom sector.
Must be registered with state handloom department.
Yarn subsidy: individual weavers and cooperatives.
Cluster development: geographical clusters.
notes: Yarn subsidy of 15–20% on supply through designated agencies.
India Handloom Brand certification fetches 20–30% premium in market.
Block-level Handloom Development Officers are key contact points.
PM Vishwakarma scheme now covers some weavers.

scheme_name: PM SVANidhi — Street Vendor Digital Loans
description: Enhanced PM SVANidhi with digital payment incentive of ₹1,200/year and credit enhancement for diligent repayers. 60+ Lakh vendors covered.
procedure: Step 1: Repay ₹10,000 first cycle SVANidhi loan timely.
Step 2: Ensure minimum 50 digital transactions per month via UPI.
Step 3: Apply for second cycle (₹20,000) through same bank/MFI.
Step 4: Bank verifies repayment history and digital transaction data.
Step 5: ₹20,000 loan sanctioned and disbursed.
Step 6: Repay and apply for third cycle ₹50,000 on timely completion.
Step 7: Continue earning digital transaction cashback (₹50/month for 100+ transactions).
eligibility_criteria: Street vendor who has repaid ₹10,000 first SVANidhi loan on time.
Active UPI digital payment usage with 50+ monthly transactions.
Must have ULB vending certificate.
Urban local body area resident.
notes: Digital payment cashback: ₹50/month for 50–99 UPI transactions; ₹100/month for 100+ transactions.
Escalating credit rewards good behavior — crucial to maintain timely repayments and digital habits.

description: ₹7,522 Crore fund for inland and marine fishery enterprises through cooperative and commercial banks. Covers boats, nets, fish farms.
procedure: Step 1: Prepare project report for fishery/aquaculture activity.
Step 2: Approach NABARD-linked bank for term loan.
Step 3: Bank appraises project and forwards to NABARD for refinance/subsidy.
Step 4: NABARD sanctions refinance; bank disburses loan.
Step 5: Implement project with regular reporting to bank.
Step 6: NABARD releases back-ended capital subsidy on project completion.
Step 7: Repay loan over agreed tenure (5–7 years typically).
eligibility_criteria: Individual fish farmers, SHGs, FPOs, cooperatives, companies in fisheries/aquaculture.
Must have suitable land/water body.
Marine fishers: valid registration with Fisheries Department.
Loan from commercial bank/RRB/cooperative bank/NABARD.
notes: NABARD's Fisheries Fund is ₹7,522 crore allocated under PMMSY (PM Matsya Sampada Yojana).
Capital subsidy: 40% (general) and 60% (SC/ST/women) of project cost.
Apply through NABARD-linked bank — not NABARD directly.

scheme_name: PLI Scheme — Specialty Chemicals & White Goods
description: PLI for specialty chemicals and white goods (ACs, LED lights) manufacturing. Target ₹25,000 Crore investments and 6 Lakh jobs.
procedure: Step 1: Check DPIIT/DPIIT sector ministry guidelines for white goods or specialty chemicals PLI.
Step 2: Register and apply on PLI portal during open application window.
Step 3: Submit investment plan, base year data, and product specifications.
Step 4: Application evaluated by ministry; inspection of manufacturing facility.
Step 5: Approval with product lines and incentive conditions specified.
Step 6: Commence production; submit quarterly/annual sales data.
Step 7: PLI incentive calculated on incremental sales; released annually.
eligibility_criteria: AC and LED Light manufacturers: minimum investment ₹1 crore (components) or ₹50 crore (finished products).
Specialty chemicals: investment commitment per product category.
Must be Indian-incorporated entity.
Linked to specific product lines.
notes: White Goods PLI: incentive 4%–6% for 5 years.
Check DPIIT notification for current open application windows.
Component manufacturers have lower threshold.
Scheme aims to develop domestic component ecosystem.

description: Supports innovative ideas through incubation, mentoring, prototype development, and market access. 300+ startups supported annually.
procedure: Step 1: Identify nearest MSME Technology Centre (TC) at msmetc.gov.in.
Step 2: Contact TC for incubation/product development inquiry.
Step 3: Submit innovation proposal to TC management.
Step 4: TC evaluates technical feasibility and commercial potential.
Step 5: Incubation agreement signed; access to TC lab, equipment, and expert guidance.
Step 6: Prototype developed with TC support; testing and certification done.
Step 7: Product commercialization with market linkage support.
eligibility_criteria: Manufacturing MSME with Udyam Registration having an innovative product/process.
Access to MSME Technology Centre for prototype development.
Testing and certification services for MSME products.
notes: 18 MSME Technology Centres across India (Aurangabad, Bhubaneswar, Indore, Jamshedpur, etc.).
Services include CNC training, die making, product testing, and metrology.
Charges are subsidised for MSMEs.
Check specific TC for incubation slots availability.

scheme_name: ECGC NIRVIK — Niryat Rin Vikas Yojana
description: Enhanced credit guarantee for MSME exporters reducing bank risk and improving credit availability. Covers pre and post-shipment credit.
procedure: Step 1: Inform your bank about ECGC NIRVIK; bank applies to ECGC for cover.
Step 2: Bank registers with ECGC for NIRVIK policy.
Step 3: Bank pays ECGC premium (cost passed to exporter as part of loan terms).
Step 4: Exporter receives bank credit with ECGC cover — no direct ECGC interaction needed.
Step 5: In case of exporter default, bank files claim with ECGC (not exporter's concern directly).
Step 6: ECGC pays 90% of bank's loss — encouraging bank to extend more credit.
Step 7: Exporter benefits from easier credit access due to ECGC cover comfort.
eligibility_criteria: Indian exporters with export credit from any scheduled bank.
ECGC cover taken by bank on behalf of exporter.
MSE exporters with annual bank credit up to ₹250 crore eligible.
IEC mandatory.
notes: NIRVIK is primarily a bank-side scheme — exporters benefit indirectly through easier credit.
ECGC covers 90% of principal and interest loss.
Banks enrolled in NIRVIK offer lower collateral requirements to MSE exporters.

description: Flexible revolving credit for farmers and agri-MSMEs for crop production, allied activities, and post-harvest storage. 7.5 Crore KCC issued.
procedure: Step 1: Apply at any bank branch (commercial bank, cooperative bank, RRB) with land documents.
Step 2: Fill KCC application form with land/crop details.
Step 3: Bank assesses credit limit based on crop production cost.
Step 4: KCC issued as ATM-cum-debit card linked to savings account.
Step 5: Use KCC at ATM or through cheque for agricultural inputs.
Step 6: Repay within crop season (6–12 months) to avail interest subvention (2% p.a.).
Step 7: Renew KCC annually with updated crop/land details.
eligibility_criteria: All farmers (owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers).
Allied sector: fishers, fish farmers, poultry and animal husbandry entrepreneurs.
No income ceiling.
Credit limit based on cultivated land and crop mix.
notes: Interest subvention: 2% for crop loans; additional 3% for timely repayment (effectively 4% net).
Enhanced KCC for fisheries up to ₹2 lakh.
Animal husbandry KCC for milk, poultry, piggery up to ₹2 lakh.
No processing fee for KCC up to ₹3 lakh.

description: Small working capital loans for very small enterprises through NSIC-empanelled MFIs and SFBs at competitive rates.
procedure: Step 1: Visit nsic.co.in or NSIC branch; apply for micro enterprise loan.
Step 2: Submit business documents, Udyam registration, and financial details.
Step 3: NSIC assesses creditworthiness through partner NBFC/bank.
Step 4: Loan sanctioned; NSIC provides partial guarantee/support.
Step 5: Disburse loan; repay through EMI over agreed period.
Step 6: Use loan for machinery, equipment, or working capital.
eligibility_criteria: Micro manufacturing enterprises with Udyam Registration.
Annual turnover up to ₹5 crore.
No NPA or wilful default.
Must have basic business documentation.
notes: NSIC acts as aggregator and facilitator for micro enterprise credit.
Interest rates vary by partner institution.
NSIC charges nominal service fee.
Also provides credit linkage under MUDRA through NSIC channel.

description: ₹120 Crore PLI for drone and drone component manufacturers. Targets ₹900 Crore turnover and 10,000 jobs in 3 years.
procedure: Step 1: Check MoCA (Ministry of Civil Aviation) PLI Drone scheme guidelines.
Step 2: Obtain DGCA type certificate for drone products.
Step 3: Register on PLI portal and submit application during open window.
Step 4: Ministry of Civil Aviation evaluates application.
Step 5: Approval letter issued with incentive conditions.
Step 6: Commence manufacturing; submit quarterly production and sales data.
Step 7: PLI incentive (20% of value addition) released annually for 3 years.
eligibility_criteria: Indian-incorporated drone/drone component manufacturer.
Products must have DGCA type certificate or component approval.
Minimum investment: ₹2 crore (drone) or ₹50 lakh (component).
PLI on value addition (domestic value addition per unit).
notes: Drone PLI is unique — 20% incentive on value addition (not turnover). 3-year scheme.
DGCA certification mandatory.
India's drone policy 2021 supports this ecosystem.
Both drone makers and component suppliers eligible.

description: Supports grassroots innovators to develop prototypes from validated grassroots innovations. Bridge between innovation and product development.
procedure: Step 1: Visit DST PRAYAS portal (dst.gov.in/prayas) for open call.
Step 2: Submit concept proposal with technology description and prototype plan.
Step 3: DST scientific committee reviews proposals.
Step 4: Shortlisted innovators invited for presentation.
Step 5: Grant agreement with PRAYAS coordinator (empanelled IITs/institutions).
Step 6: Prototype development at host institution with DST funding.
Step 7: Technology demonstration and report submission.
eligibility_criteria: Individual innovator, research scholar, or scientist in physical science/engineering.
Must be Indian citizen.
Must have a novel technology concept at prototype stage.
Preferably associated with academic institution or R&D lab.
notes: PRAYAS is for physical sciences (materials, sensors, devices, instrumentation).
Grant up to ₹10 lakh for 18 months.
Implemented through empanelled technical institutions (IITs, IISERs, NITs).
Calls issued 2–3 times annually.

scheme_name: Integrated Cold Chain & Value Addition Infrastructure
description: Subsidises cold chain infrastructure from farm gate to consumer. Covers pre-cooling, packing houses, reefer transport, and cold stores.
procedure: Step 1: Develop integrated cold chain project proposal covering pre-cooling, storage, processing, and transport.
Step 2: Apply on MoFPI PMKSY portal during open application round.
Step 3: Submit DPR, land documents, environmental clearances.
Step 4: MoFPI/Project Management Agency appraised project.
Step 5: Approval issued; project implementation begins.
Step 6: Submit claims with invoices and physical verification.
Step 7: Grant released in instalments: 35% after foundation, 50% mid-project, 15% completion.
eligibility_criteria: Private companies, cooperatives, FPOs, SHGs.
End-to-end cold chain project (pre-cooling to retail-ready).
Minimum project cost ₹50 lakh.
FSSAI licence required.
Must link to farm produce.
notes: Grant: 35% of project cost (max ₹10 crore).
NE/hilly states: 50% subsidy.
Must maintain integrated cold chain — no break in temperature throughout.
Refrigerated transport and processing must be linked to primary production.

scheme_name: NITI Aayog AIM Atal Tinkering Labs
description: Innovation workspaces in schools and colleges with 3D printers, robotics, IoT kits. 10,000+ ATLs created. Fosters STEM entrepreneurship.
procedure: Step 1: School applies on ATL portal (aim.gov.in/atl) during open application window.
Step 2: Submit school profile, facility details, and ATL implementation plan.
Step 3: AIM evaluates application; shortlists schools based on selection criteria.
