Step 4: Selected schools receive grant intimation: ₹20 lakh total (₹10 lakh establishment + ₹10 lakh operation over 5 years).
Step 5: School sets up ATL with approved equipment list.
Step 6: AIM provides mentors and training for ATL in-charges.
Step 7: Students engage in maker projects, competitions, and innovation challenges.
eligibility_criteria: Schools (government, aided, private) from Class 6–12.
CBSE/ICSE or state board affiliation.
Must have dedicated ATL space (1500–2000 sq ft).
School must commit to infrastructure maintenance.
Apply via online portal.
notes: ATL is for school innovation education — not a business scheme.
Over 10,000 ATLs established across India.
Schools must maintain activity logs and submit annual reports to AIM.
ATL Annual Challenge allows student innovations to get funding.

description: Long-term project finance for export-oriented manufacturing units at competitive rates. Supports capacity creation for global markets.
procedure: Step 1: Secure overseas project contract and approach EXIM Bank.
Step 2: Submit project details, contract documents, and financial projections.
Step 3: EXIM Bank appraises project viability and risk.
Step 4: Sanction of project finance/buyer's credit/line of credit.
Step 5: EXIM Bank disburses finance directly to contractor or buyer country.
Step 6: Indian exporter/contractor receives payment from buyer with EXIM Bank guarantee.
Step 7: Repayment through project revenues over agreed tenor.
eligibility_criteria: Indian contractor/company with confirmed overseas project contract.
Construction, engineering, consultancy, or supply contracts with foreign government/entity.
No minimum size — tailored to project requirements.
notes: EXIM Bank also provides Lines of Credit (LoC) to foreign governments to buy Indian goods/services — connecting Indian exporters to overseas government buyers.
Check EXIM Bank country-wise LoC programs.

description: Facilitates startups to access international markets through trade missions, global events, and bilateral startup bridges with 50+ countries.
procedure: Step 1: Register on Startup India Hub (startupindia.gov.in).
Step 2: Apply for specific international programme: India-Israel Bridge, India-UK Bridge, India-US Startup Bridge, etc.
Step 3: Submit startup profile, product description, and international expansion plan.
Step 4: Selection committee evaluates applications.
Step 5: Selected startups participate in delegation, exchange visits, or soft landing programmes.
Step 6: Access market entry support: business matchmaking, regulatory guidance.
Step 7: Leverage Startup India international network for investor and partnership connections.
documents_required: Letter of intent from overseas partner (if any)
eligibility_criteria: DPIIT-recognised startup with validated product/service.
Ready for international expansion.
Sector-agnostic but preference to deep-tech, sustainability, and export potential startups.
notes: Startup Bridge programs with Israel, Finland, Japan, UK, US, South Korea active.
Apply for specific country bridges with relevant sector focus.
Also access Startup20 G20 opportunities through Startup India.

scheme_name: KVIC Prime Minister Employment Generation (PMEGP) — Artisan
description: KVIC-channel PMEGP for village and artisan industries with special focus on khadi, handloom, and traditional products.
procedure: Step 1: Apply online at kviconline.gov.in/pmegpeportal selecting KVIC channel.
Step 2: Select khadi or village industry category.
Step 3: KVIC district office scrutinizes application and conducts interview.
Step 4: DLTFC approval and bank linkage.
Step 5: EDP training completion (mandatory).
Step 6: Margin money subsidy released by KVIC to bank on project implementation.
Step 7: Enterprise established; artisan receives market linkage support from KVIC.
eligibility_criteria: Individual artisan above 18 years.
Must be from traditional craft/artisan community.
Project in village or cottage industry sector.
Education: 8th pass for projects above ₹10 lakh.
SHGs and artisan cooperatives eligible.
notes: KVIC has artisan clusters and exhibitions (India International Trade Fair) for market linkage.
Khadi Mark certification available post-establishment.
KVIC also procures artisan products for government gifting programme.

description: Creates modern agricultural marketing infrastructure with storage, grading, and market yards. Targets 22,000 GrAMs.
procedure: Step 1: State government/SAMB submits proposal to NABARD.
Step 2: NABARD appraises project and market infrastructure plan.
Step 3: Long-term soft loan sanctioned to state government (7% p.a., 10-year repayment).
Step 4: State implements market infrastructure projects.
Step 5: Individual agri-entrepreneurs benefit through improved market access.
Step 6: FPOs can apply for infrastructure at their level through state SAMB.
eligibility_criteria: State governments, state agricultural marketing boards, FPOs/cooperatives for community infrastructure.
Individual agri-business units not directly eligible — benefits flow through state schemes.
Preference to states with liberal APMC Act reform.
notes: AMIF is primarily a state-to-NABARD lending programme.
Individual entrepreneurs benefit through improved markets, not direct grants.
Contact your State Agricultural Marketing Board (SAMB) for any parallel state-level market infrastructure grants.

description: Startups can close company in 90 days via STK-2 fast track exit without paying accumulated taxes up to ₹10 Lakh.
procedure: Step 1: Board of Directors passes resolution to wind up company.
Step 2: File Form NESL-1 on MCA21 portal (mca.gov.in) for voluntary winding up.
Step 3: DPIIT-recognised startups file simplified application with declaration of solvency.
Step 4: Pay off all creditors; obtain NOCs from banks and tax departments.
Step 5: Submit final accounts and utilization statements.
Step 6: NCLT (National Company Law Tribunal) approves winding up if no objections.
Step 7: Company struck off; promoters receive remaining assets.
eligibility_criteria: DPIIT-recognised startup.
No outstanding liabilities to any creditor.
No pending legal proceedings.
Company must file declaration of solvency.
Applicable for companies under Companies Act 2013.
notes: Fast-track winding up enables closure in 90 days vs 2–3 years conventionally.
All debts must be cleared before filing.
Promoters can restart a new venture without the burden of the old company.
This reduces entrepreneurship risk.

description: 18 Technology Centres across India with advanced CNC machines, 3D printers, testing labs. Subsidised access for MSME prototyping and production.
procedure: Step 1: Identify nearest MSME Technology Centre at msmetc.gov.in.
Step 2: Contact TC for specific service required (job work, testing, training).
Step 3: Submit service request with technical specifications.
Step 4: TC provides cost estimate (subsidized rates for MSMEs).
Step 5: Sign service agreement; provide raw material if needed.
Step 6: TC delivers service within agreed timeline.
Step 7: Receive finished product, test report, or training certificate.
eligibility_criteria: Any MSME (manufacturing/service) needing advanced manufacturing or testing services.
Individual entrepreneurs and students for skill development programmes.
No restriction on sector for service availing.
notes: TCs offer CNC machining, die casting, forging, press shop, design services.
Testing includes material testing, environmental testing, electrical testing.
Skill training in precision manufacturing, mechatronics, etc.
Rates are 20–40% lower than market for MSMEs.

scheme_name: PM MUDRA — Mahila Udyam Nidhi Scheme
description: Special MUDRA-linked soft loan for women entrepreneurs at below prime lending rate. Concessional rate for 5 years.
procedure: Step 1: Apply at SIDBI branch or PSU bank participating in Mahila Udyam Nidhi.
Step 2: Submit business plan, financial projections, and personal documents.
Step 3: Bank/SIDBI appraises the proposal; emphasis on women entrepreneur track record.
Step 4: Soft loan of up to ₹10 lakh sanctioned.
Step 5: Repay over 10 years with 5-year moratorium.
Step 6: Use loan for capital equipment, working capital, or technology.
eligibility_criteria: Women entrepreneurs (51%+ ownership).
Tiny/small sector manufacturing or service enterprise.
Udyam registered.
Business with growth potential.
Not an NPA.
notes: Mahila Udyam Nidhi is a quasi-equity / soft loan product.
Interest rate: 1% below PLR.
Repayment 10 years with 5-year moratorium makes EMI very low.
Ideal for women entrepreneurs needing patient capital for growth.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Jan Aushadhi Kendra Franchise
description: Franchise for Jan Aushadhi generic medicine stores. Setup grant, preferential medicine supply, and margin of 20% on MRP.
procedure: Step 1: Apply online on janaushadhi.gov.in.
Step 2: Submit application with pharmacist registration, space details, and bank account.
Step 3: BPPI (Bureau of Pharma PSU of India) reviews application.
Step 4: Provisional allotment letter issued after verification.
Step 5: Set up store with BPPI-approved furniture and branding.
Step 6: Open store; purchase medicines from BPPI at wholesale rates.
Step 7: Earn 15% margin on MRP; receive ₹2.5 lakh incentive (over 12 months or after ₹2.5 lakh purchase).
eligibility_criteria: Individual: must be registered pharmacist or have pharmacist on payroll.
NGOs, hospitals, and SHGs also eligible.
Must have retail space of minimum 120 sq ft.
For NE/Himalayan states, SC/ST, women: additional ₹1.5 lakh incentive.
notes: ₹2.5 lakh incentive = ₹15,000/month for first 12 months after store setup.
Special incentive of ₹1.5 lakh additional for NE, SC/ST, women, differently-abled applicants.
Medicines include 1,700+ generics at 50–90% discount.
Steady monthly footfall from day one.

scheme_name: National Tribal Finance & Dev Corp — ST Entrepreneur Loan
description: Concessional finance to tribal communities for income-generating activities. Special schemes for women tribal entrepreneurs and forest produce MSMEs.
procedure: Step 1: Approach State Channelizing Agency (State Tribal Finance Corporation) in your state.
Step 2: Obtain application form and fill with project details.
Step 3: Submit with ST certificate, income proof, and project proposal.
Step 4: SCA evaluates and forwards to NSTFDC.
Step 5: NSTFDC sanctions; SCA disburses to beneficiary.
Step 6: Repay in quarterly installments over 5 years.
eligibility_criteria: Must be ST community member.
Annual family income ≤₹3 lakh.
Age 18–55 years.
Viable income-generating project.
Not availed similar benefit previously.
Priority to women, physically challenged.
notes: Apply through State Tribal Finance Corporation — not directly to NSTFDC.
Loan limit: ₹30 lakh for term loan; ₹10 lakh for education.
Interest: 6% general, 5% for women.
Education loan for professional courses also available.

scheme_name: SIDBI Venture Capital Early Stage Fund
description: SIDBI's venture capital fund investing in scalable startups with social impact and technology focus. Portfolio of 100+ startups.
procedure: Step 1: Apply on SIDBI Startup Mitra portal or connect via Startup India ecosystem.
Step 2: Submit pitch deck, business plan, financials, and team profile.
Step 3: SIDBI VC team reviews; shortlisted startups invited for presentation.
Step 4: Due diligence: financial, legal, technical, and market assessment.
Step 5: Investment committee approval; term sheet issued.
Step 6: Legal documentation (SHA, SSA); board representation as per terms.
Step 7: Funds disbursed; SIDBI provides mentorship and ecosystem support.
eligibility_criteria: DPIIT-recognised startup.
Early to growth stage (seed to Series A).
Technology-driven, scalable business.
Indian incorporated entity.
Preference to manufacturing, deep-tech, sustainability, and social impact sectors.
notes: SIDBI VC is a patient, government-backed investor — less pressure than private VC.
Ticket size: ₹1–10 crore.
Takes minority equity stake.
Also participates as anchor LP in other VC funds.
Processing takes 3–6 months for full due diligence.

description: Facilitates SC/ST enterprises to access government procurement through mentoring, capacity building, and handholding for 4% procurement mandate.
procedure: Step 1: Register on National SC-ST Hub portal (scsthub.in).
Step 2: Complete business profile including products, capabilities, and certifications.
Step 3: Enroll in vendor development and capacity building programmes offered by NSSH.
Step 4: Apply for government procurement opportunities via NSSH market linkage cell.
Step 5: Participate in Buyer-Seller Meets organized by NSSH.
Step 6: Link to GeM portal with NSSH support; avail SC/ST enterprise preference.
Step 7: Access mentoring from corporates empanelled with NSSH.
eligibility_criteria: MSMEs with majority SC/ST ownership (>51%).
Valid Udyam Registration.
Enrolled on National SC-ST Hub portal.
Products/services suitable for government or corporate procurement.
notes: Government policy mandates 4% procurement from SC/ST enterprises.
NSSH connects SC/ST MSMEs with government buyers and CPSEs.
Also provides Special CLCSS (25% subsidy) for technology upgradation.
Registration on scsthub.in is free.

scheme_name: EXIM Bank MSME Overseas Investment Finance
description: Supports Indian MSMEs to set up overseas marketing offices, joint ventures, and wholly-owned subsidiaries for export market development.
procedure: Step 1: Obtain RBI ODI approval for overseas investment.
Step 2: Approach EXIM Bank with overseas investment proposal.
Step 3: Submit business plan, financial statements, and JV agreement.
Step 4: EXIM Bank appraises investment viability and export promotion impact.
Step 5: Loan sanctioned in INR or foreign currency.
Step 6: Invest in overseas entity as per RBI guidelines.
Step 7: Repay from dividend income or export revenue.
eligibility_criteria: Indian MSME seeking to invest in overseas JV or subsidiary.
Investment must promote Indian exports or technology acquisition.
RBI approval for ODI (Overseas Direct Investment) required.
Business plan with overseas investment rationale.

description: Capital subsidy for MSMEs installing rooftop solar with net metering benefits and accelerated depreciation.
procedure: Step 1 — Check Solar Potential: Assess your facility's rooftop area, power consumption (latest electricity bill), and grid connectivity.
Step 2 — Register on State Solar Portal: Visit https://msmetamilnadu.tn.gov.in or the state energy agency website (e.g., TEDA for TN, PEDA for Punjab, HAREDA for Haryana).
Step 3 — Apply for Grid-Connected Solar: Apply for net metering through the state DISCOM (electricity distribution company). Submit application with premises and load details.
Step 4 — Technical Feasibility: State agency or DISCOM conducts site inspection for shadow-free area and grid capacity.
Step 5 — Select Empanelled Vendor: Choose a state-empanelled solar vendor. Obtain detailed quotation for recommended system size.

Step 7 — Installation by Vendor: Empanelled vendor installs the solar system. DISCOM provides net metering connection.
Step 8 — Start Generating and Saving: Solar generation offsets DISCOM bill. Excess units credited at DISCOM feed-in tariff. Payback in 4–6 years.

scheme_name: Gujarat Solar for MSMEs — Suryashakti Scheme
description: Capital subsidy and accelerated depreciation for solar rooftop installations in MSME units with net metering connection.
procedure: Step 1 — Check Solar Potential: Assess your facility's rooftop area, power consumption (latest electricity bill), and grid connectivity.
Step 2 — Register on State Solar Portal: Visit https://ic.gujarat.gov.in or the state energy agency website (e.g., TEDA for TN, PEDA for Punjab, HAREDA for Haryana).
Step 3 — Apply for Grid-Connected Solar: Apply for net metering through the state DISCOM (electricity distribution company). Submit application with premises and load details.
Step 4 — Technical Feasibility: State agency or DISCOM conducts site inspection for shadow-free area and grid capacity.
Step 5 — Select Empanelled Vendor: Choose a state-empanelled solar vendor. Obtain detailed quotation for recommended system size.
Step 6 — Apply for Subsidy: Submit subsidy application to the state energy agency. Central PM Surya Ghar subsidy may also apply.
Step 7 — Installation by Vendor: Empanelled vendor installs the solar system. DISCOM provides net metering connection.
Step 8 — Start Generating and Saving: Solar generation offsets DISCOM bill. Excess units credited at DISCOM feed-in tariff. Payback in 4–6 years.

description: Rooftop solar capital subsidy for MSMEs in Andhra Pradesh with net metering connection.
procedure: Step 1 — Check Solar Potential: Assess your facility's rooftop area, power consumption (latest electricity bill), and grid connectivity.
Step 2 — Register on State Solar Portal: Visit https://www.apindustries.gov.in or the state energy agency website (e.g., TEDA for TN, PEDA for Punjab, HAREDA for Haryana).
Step 3 — Apply for Grid-Connected Solar: Apply for net metering through the state DISCOM (electricity distribution company). Submit application with premises and load details.
Step 4 — Technical Feasibility: State agency or DISCOM conducts site inspection for shadow-free area and grid capacity.
Step 5 — Select Empanelled Vendor: Choose a state-empanelled solar vendor. Obtain detailed quotation for recommended system size.
Step 6 — Apply for Subsidy: Submit subsidy application to the state energy agency. Central PM Surya Ghar subsidy may also apply.
Step 7 — Installation by Vendor: Empanelled vendor installs the solar system. DISCOM provides net metering connection.
Step 8 — Start Generating and Saving: Solar generation offsets DISCOM bill. Excess units credited at DISCOM feed-in tariff. Payback in 4–6 years.

description: Capital subsidy for rooftop solar with net metering for MSME units in West Bengal.
procedure: Step 1 — Check Solar Potential: Assess your facility's rooftop area, power consumption (latest electricity bill), and grid connectivity.
Step 2 — Register on State Solar Portal: Visit https://wbmsme.gov.in or the state energy agency website (e.g., TEDA for TN, PEDA for Punjab, HAREDA for Haryana).
Step 3 — Apply for Grid-Connected Solar: Apply for net metering through the state DISCOM (electricity distribution company). Submit application with premises and load details.
Step 4 — Technical Feasibility: State agency or DISCOM conducts site inspection for shadow-free area and grid capacity.
Step 5 — Select Empanelled Vendor: Choose a state-empanelled solar vendor. Obtain detailed quotation for recommended system size.
Step 6 — Apply for Subsidy: Submit subsidy application to the state energy agency. Central PM Surya Ghar subsidy may also apply.

description: Capital subsidy for rooftop solar installations in MSME units across Uttar Pradesh with net metering.
procedure: Step 1 — Check Solar Potential: Assess your facility's rooftop area, power consumption (latest electricity bill), and grid connectivity.
Step 2 — Register on State Solar Portal: Visit https://msme.up.gov.in or the state energy agency website (e.g., TEDA for TN, PEDA for Punjab, HAREDA for Haryana).
Step 3 — Apply for Grid-Connected Solar: Apply for net metering through the state DISCOM (electricity distribution company). Submit application with premises and load details.
Step 4 — Technical Feasibility: State agency or DISCOM conducts site inspection for shadow-free area and grid capacity.
Step 5 — Select Empanelled Vendor: Choose a state-empanelled solar vendor. Obtain detailed quotation for recommended system size.
Step 6 — Apply for Subsidy: Submit subsidy application to the state energy agency. Central PM Surya Ghar subsidy may also apply.
Step 7 — Installation by Vendor: Empanelled vendor installs the solar system. DISCOM provides net metering connection.
Step 8 — Start Generating and Saving: Solar generation offsets DISCOM bill. Excess units credited at DISCOM feed-in tariff. Payback in 4–6 years.

Step 2 — Get Udyam Registration: Register FREE at https://udyamregistration.gov.in.
Step 3 — Prepare Complete Documents: Gather identity proof, business registration, financial statements, and project report.
Step 4 — Register on State/Scheme Portal: Visit https://udyami.bihar.gov.in → create applicant account → complete your business profile.
Step 5 — Fill and Submit Application: Complete the scheme application form with accurate information. Attach all documents.
Step 6 — Application Verification: Implementing authority verifies your application and documents. Physical inspection may be done.
Step 7 — Approval by Competent Authority: Committee/officer reviews and approves eligible applications.
Step 8 — Receive Benefit: Approved incentive, subsidy, or benefit delivered to your registered bank account or enterprise directly.
documents_required: Bank account details with IFSC (cancelled cheque)
Proof of Bihar domicile/residency (ration card / voter ID)
eligibility_criteria: SC/ST, Women, EBC youth aged 18–50 in Bihar
Enterprise must be established in Bihar
notes: Contact your nearest District Industries Centre (DIC) in Bihar for in-person application guidance and processing.
Udyam Registration is free and mandatory — complete it at https://udyamregistration.gov.in before applying for any scheme.
Maintain GST compliance and proper books of accounts — subsidy claims may be rejected for non-compliant enterprises.
Check https://udyami.bihar.gov.in regularly for latest scheme guidelines, updated application windows, and notifications.

description: Solar rooftop capital subsidy for MSME units in Bihar to reduce power costs.
procedure: Step 1 — Check Solar Potential: Assess your facility's rooftop area, power consumption (latest electricity bill), and grid connectivity.
Step 2 — Register on State Solar Portal: Visit https://udyami.bihar.gov.in or the state energy agency website (e.g., TEDA for TN, PEDA for Punjab, HAREDA for Haryana).
Step 3 — Apply for Grid-Connected Solar: Apply for net metering through the state DISCOM (electricity distribution company). Submit application with premises and load details.
Step 4 — Technical Feasibility: State agency or DISCOM conducts site inspection for shadow-free area and grid capacity.
Step 5 — Select Empanelled Vendor: Choose a state-empanelled solar vendor. Obtain detailed quotation for recommended system size.
Step 6 — Apply for Subsidy: Submit subsidy application to the state energy agency. Central PM Surya Ghar subsidy may also apply.
Step 7 — Installation by Vendor: Empanelled vendor installs the solar system. DISCOM provides net metering connection.
Step 8 — Start Generating and Saving: Solar generation offsets DISCOM bill. Excess units credited at DISCOM feed-in tariff. Payback in 4–6 years.

description: State seed fund for early-stage startups in Jharkhand with incubation at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad.
procedure: Step 1 — Get DPIIT Startup Recognition: Visit https://www.startupindia.gov.in → 'Get Recognised' → fill details → submit. FREE, takes 2–3 days.

Step 7 — Milestone Reporting: Submit quarterly progress reports. Subsequent tranches released on achieving agreed milestones.
Step 8 — Demo Day and Investor Access: Participate in state-level Demo Day to access investors and strategic partners.

Step 2 — Register with State Agency: Visit https://himachalindustries.nic.in and register your startup with the Himachal Pradesh startup/MSME agency.
Step 3 — Apply to Empanelled Incubator/Programme: Find empanelled incubators on the state portal and apply with pitch deck and business plan.
Step 4 — Submit Application Package: Include: pitch deck (12–15 slides), 3-year financial model, MVP demo, team CVs, and cap table.
Step 5 — Evaluation Round: Selection committee evaluates innovation, market potential, team, and traction. May call for in-person pitch.
Step 6 — Agreement and Seed Fund Access: Selected startups sign funding/incubation agreement. Seed fund released in milestone-based tranches.
Step 7 — Milestone Reporting: Submit quarterly progress reports. Subsequent tranches released on achieving agreed milestones.
Step 8 — Demo Day and Investor Access: Participate in state-level Demo Day to access investors and strategic partners.
documents_required: Bank account details with IFSC (cancelled cheque)
Proof of Himachal Pradesh domicile/residency (ration card / voter ID)
eligibility_criteria: Rural tourism entrepreneurs in HP
DPIIT Startup Recognition mandatory
Innovation-driven product/service with scalability
Annual turnover not exceeding ₹100 Crore
Enterprise must be established in Himachal Pradesh
notes: Contact your nearest District Industries Centre (DIC) in Himachal Pradesh for in-person application guidance and processing.
Udyam Registration is free and mandatory — complete it at https://udyamregistration.gov.in before applying for any scheme.
Maintain GST compliance and proper books of accounts — subsidy claims may be rejected for non-compliant enterprises.
Check https://himachalindustries.nic.in regularly for latest scheme guidelines, updated application windows, and notifications.

description: Solar rooftop capital subsidy for MSME units in Uttarakhand with net metering.
procedure: Step 1 — Check Solar Potential: Assess your facility's rooftop area, power consumption (latest electricity bill), and grid connectivity.
Step 2 — Register on State Solar Portal: Visit https://siidcul.com or the state energy agency website (e.g., TEDA for TN, PEDA for Punjab, HAREDA for Haryana).
Step 3 — Apply for Grid-Connected Solar: Apply for net metering through the state DISCOM (electricity distribution company). Submit application with premises and load details.
Step 4 — Technical Feasibility: State agency or DISCOM conducts site inspection for shadow-free area and grid capacity.
Step 5 — Select Empanelled Vendor: Choose a state-empanelled solar vendor. Obtain detailed quotation for recommended system size.
Step 6 — Apply for Subsidy: Submit subsidy application to the state energy agency. Central PM Surya Ghar subsidy may also apply.
Step 7 — Installation by Vendor: Empanelled vendor installs the solar system. DISCOM provides net metering connection.
Step 8 — Start Generating and Saving: Solar generation offsets DISCOM bill. Excess units credited at DISCOM feed-in tariff. Payback in 4–6 years.

description: State seed grants for early-stage innovation startups in Mizoram.

Step 6 — Agreement and Seed Fund Access: Selected startups sign funding/incubation agreement. Seed fund released in milestone-based tranches.
Step 7 — Milestone Reporting: Submit quarterly progress reports. Subsequent tranches released on achieving agreed milestones.

scheme_name: Kotak Mahindra Bank MSME Business Loan
description: Digital business loans for established MSMEs with quick turnaround and competitive interest rates.
procedure: Step 1 — Visit Bank Website or Branch: Go to the bank's official MSME/Business Banking section online or visit nearest branch.
Step 2 — Check Eligibility: Review the specific loan product eligibility criteria — turnover, CIBIL score, and collateral requirements.
Step 3 — Prepare Loan File: Compile: Udyam Registration, GST returns (last 6–12 months), bank statements (last 12 months), audited financials, and project report.
Step 4 — Apply Online or at Branch: Submit application through the bank's online MSME loan portal or at the branch's MSME desk.
Step 5 — Bank Credit Appraisal: Bank evaluates CIBIL score (target 700+), financial health, business vintage, and repayment capacity.
Step 6 — Loan Sanction Letter: Bank issues sanction letter with loan amount, interest rate, tenure, and EMI schedule.
Step 7 — Documentation and Agreement: Sign loan agreement. Provide post-dated cheques or ECS mandate for EMI.
Step 8 — Disbursement: Loan disbursed to your current account. Interest starts from disbursement date. Repay EMIs on due date.
